about: Sourced life stories for the prophets of the wilderness and the judges who had none: Miriam, Eldad and Medad. Written from Scripture and the dossier Research/People/prophets-wilderness-judges.md.

miriam-exo-15-20.short: The sister of Aaron and Moses, called "the prophetess", who led the women’s song at the sea and died at Kadesh.

paragraphs.text: Miriam was a child of Amram and Jochebed; Numbers and Chronicles name the three together: Aaron, Moses and Miriam. When the baby Moses was laid among the flags by the river, "his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him", and offered to fetch a Hebrew nurse. Exodus does not give that sister’s name.

After Israel crossed the sea and Moses and the people sang to the LORD, "Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand", and all the women went out after her with timbrels and dances. She answered them with the opening words of the song: "Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea."

At Hazeroth Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman he had married, and asked, "Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us?" The LORD called the three of them to the tabernacle and said that with Moses he spoke "mouth to mouth". When the cloud lifted, Miriam was "leprous, white as snow". Aaron pleaded for her, Moses cried to the LORD to heal her, and she was shut out of the camp seven days; the people did not move on until she was brought in again.

Miriam died at Kadesh in the desert of Zin and was buried there. Deuteronomy later told Israel to "Remember what the LORD thy God did unto Miriam by the way", and Micah names her with her brothers: "I sent before thee Moses, Aaron, and Miriam." Her words and the questions about her are set out on her prophet page.

eldad-num-11-26.short: One of two men who prophesied in the Israelite camp when the spirit rested on them; Moses would not forbid them.

paragraphs.text: Eldad is named only in one passage, with Medad. The LORD told Moses to gather seventy elders to the tabernacle, and took of the spirit that was on Moses and gave it to them. Two men had stayed in the camp: "the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the spirit rested upon them". They "went not out unto the tabernacle: and they prophesied in the camp."

A young man ran to tell Moses, and Joshua said, "My lord Moses, forbid them." Moses answered, "Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the LORD’s people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit upon them!"
Scripture says little of him. It records nothing he said, gives no family or tribe, and tells nothing more of him after this day.
